correctness.rationale: For d≥2 and t≥1, the centered product characters are orthonormal by box exactness and their isotropic second moment fixes the trace of the arclength derivative energy. The endpoint phase is common to the family; Parseval in its periodic or antiperiodic basis gives occupancies in [0,1] summing to N=(t+1)^d. Periodic even N has strictly higher minimum trace. In the other cases there is a strict squared-frequency gap beyond the lowest N modes, so equality leaves no occupancy outside this band. The extreme nonzero exponents in a constant-modulus finite Fourier series would yield a unique nonzero coefficient at their difference in the squared modulus; thus each character is a single mode. Ratios at adjacent indices and continuity force each real lift coordinate to be affine. The full band then gives distinct consecutive digit sums after sign changes. In increasing order a next weight below the length of the already filled interval duplicates a sum, and a larger one leaves a gap. This forces the radix powers. Reduction modulo t+1 proves the converse; nonzero distinct absolute coordinates give the stated signed-permutation census.
residual_risks: The winding census is diagnostic only. The analytic argument applies to normalized arclength and the standard flat metric, not weighted designs or other frequency sets.
